answer: Each agent may propose an action, but only proposals backed by a stake that is locked until independent agents verify the result earn payment. If a proposal is fraudulent, the stake is slashed and split among verifiers; creating many aliases does not multiply influence unless the attacker also funds each one, and coordinated false verification risks losing every stake. This makes a mesa of identities costly to sustain, while diverse reviewers across a canyon or grove can challenge collusion.
